Entry points and syscall numbers beyond close range flags and capability versioning are not shown.
Architecture specific byteswap hook implementations and general fallback function bodies are not shown.
Netlink family identifiers and task statistics maximum values referenced by cgroup commands are not shown.

findings.text: Big endian host conversion family preserves values when moving between host order, network order and big endian order for sixteen, thirty two and sixty four bit widths, only adjusting type annotation, while movement between host order and little endian order reverses byte order. The family offers compile time evaluable forms, ordinary value forms, pointer load forms that read from an address, and in place forms that update through a pointer.

Little endian host conversion family preserves values between host order and little endian order for sixteen, thirty two and sixty four bit widths, only adjusting annotation, while movement between host order and either network order or big endian order reverses byte order. It likewise offers compile time forms, value forms, pointer load forms and in place update forms with mirrored native versus swapping roles.

Byte reversal primitives handle sixteen, thirty two and sixty four bit values plus pointer variants. Value forms select a compiler byteswap intrinsic where the toolchain provides one, otherwise they choose a constant folding path for compile time inputs and a general function path otherwise. Pointer forms prefer an architecture specific hook when defined and otherwise load the pointed value and apply the matching value reversal.

Pointer load helpers are pure loads that return a converted value and leave memory unchanged, while in place helpers store the converted result back. Native order pointer loads dereference directly without swapping, and native order in place updates are intentional no operations that still reference their argument once for side effect safety. Foreign order variants always swap.
Little endian user interface identifies host order with decimal value 1234, provides a bitfield order marker for conditional layout, and uses a dedicated header guard to prevent double inclusion.

User space capability exchange uses a header with a thirty two bit version followed by an integer process identifier, referenced through a user address pointer alias, paired with an array of data records each holding effective, permitted and inheritable sets as thirty two bit words in that order, also referenced through a user pointer alias.

Capability protocol versions are first generation with value 0x19980330 and one word, second generation with value 0x20071026 and two words now superseded, and third generation with value 0x20080522 and two words as current. A compatibility alias selects the first generation version and word count, with a header guard against reinclusion.

On disk capability record starts with a little endian thirty two bit magic and flags word, followed by two slots each containing little endian permitted and inheritable words. The namespaced variant appends a little endian root identifier word after the slots. Array sizing follows the current two word count, with older one word and two word shapes retained for size history.

File capability encoding reserves the top byte for revision with shift 24, defines the complement as flags mask, and assigns effective flag value 1. Revisions are one, two and three in the top byte, with word counts one, two and two and extended attribute sizes derived from thirty two bit units for each generation, plus aliases selecting the third generation size, count and revision as current.

Early capabilities assign CAP_CHOWN to 0, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE to 1, CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH to 2, CAP_FOWNER to 3, CAP_FSETID to 4, CAP_KILL to 5, CAP_SETGID to 6, CAP_SETUID to 7, CAP_SETPCAP to 8 and CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE to 9.
Network and IPC capabilities assign CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE to 10, CAP_NET_BROADCAST to 11, CAP_NET_ADMIN to 12, CAP_NET_RAW to 13, CAP_IPC_LOCK to 14 and CAP_IPC_OWNER to 15.

System capabilities assign CAP_SYS_MODULE to 16, CAP_SYS_RAWIO to 17, CAP_SYS_CHROOT to 18, CAP_SYS_PTRACE to 19, CAP_SYS_PACCT to 20, CAP_SYS_ADMIN to 21, CAP_SYS_BOOT to 22, CAP_SYS_NICE to 23, CAP_SYS_RESOURCE to 24, CAP_SYS_TIME to 25 and CAP_SYS_TTY_CONFIG to 26.

Device, audit and access capabilities assign CAP_MKNOD to 27, CAP_LEASE to 28, CAP_AUDIT_WRITE to 29, CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL to 30, CAP_SETFCAP to 31, CAP_MAC_OVERRIDE to 32, CAP_MAC_ADMIN to 33, CAP_SYSLOG to 34, CAP_WAKE_ALARM to 35 and CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND to 36.

Recent capabilities assign CAP_AUDIT_READ to 37, CAP_PERFMON to 38, CAP_BPF to 39 and CAP_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE to 40, with CAP_LAST_CAP aliasing the fortieth value. Validity holds for non negative values up to that maximum, index derives by shifting right five bits, and mask derives by shifting one by the low five bits.
Control group statistics record holds five sixty four bit counters in order for sleeping, running, stopped, uninterruptible and IO wait tasks.

Control group statistics protocol reserves an unspecified command continuing from the task statistics maximum, then defines GET for user to kernel request and response plus NEW for kernel to user events, with a derived maximum. Type space reserves zero then defines group statistics payload with its own maximum, and command attributes reserve zero then define a file descriptor slot with its own maximum.
Close range control uses bit one with numeric value two for unsharing descriptor tables and bit two with numeric value four for setting close on exec, guarded against double inclusion.

Process connector subscription uses LISTEN value one and IGNORE value two, exchanged in an input record pairing an operation with an event selector. A helper narrows any selector by intersecting it with the aggregate of reportable events.

Process event bits assign PROC_EVENT_NONE to 0x00000000, PROC_EVENT_FORK to 0x00000001, PROC_EVENT_EXEC to 0x00000002, PROC_EVENT_UID to 0x00000004, PROC_EVENT_GID to 0x00000040, PROC_EVENT_SID to 0x00000080, PROC_EVENT_PTRACE to 0x00000100, PROC_EVENT_COMM to 0x00000200, PROC_EVENT_NONZERO_EXIT to 0x20000000, PROC_EVENT_COREDUMP to 0x40000000 and PROC_EVENT_EXIT to 0x80000000, with PROC_EVENT_ALL combining the reportable set.

Process event record starts with an event selector, a thirty two bit CPU number and an eight byte aligned sixty four bit boot relative timestamp in nanoseconds, followed by a trailing union. Variants carry acknowledgement error, fork parent and child process and thread group identifiers, exec process identifiers, credential change process identifiers with real and effective user or group words, session identifiers, ptrace process and tracer identifiers, command name with process identifiers and sixteen byte text, coredump process and parent identifiers, and exit process and parent identifiers with exit code and signal.

Constant helpers provide two modes. Assembler mode passes values through unchanged, while C mode pastes a suffix onto a value for sized constants and casts a value to a named type. Guards prevent reinclusion.

Sized constant helpers build unsigned long and unsigned long long literals, single bit masks of those widths by shifting one, and a one hundred twenty eight bit mask by shifting an extended integer one.

Alignment rounds a value upward to a multiple using a mask derived from one less than the alignment. Integer division helpers offer round up by adding divisor minus one before dividing, and round to nearest with sign aware adjustment adding or subtracting half the divisor based on operand signs and using common type temporaries.
Coredump handling modes occupy the low four bits with COREDUMP_KERNEL to 1, COREDUMP_USERSPACE to 2, COREDUMP_REJECT to 4 and COREDUMP_WAIT to 8, guarded against reinclusion.

Coredump request carries a thirty two bit size with a thirty two bit size acknowledgement and a sixty four bit mask, while acknowledgement carries size with spare and mask. Each publishes a version zero wire size of sixteen unsigned.

Pointer conversion helpers reinterpret little and big endian addresses as plain unsigned addresses when swapping, which relies on compatible representation and alignment. Callers must ensure the pointed object is correctly aligned and addressable, and must not assume the helpers validate sizes or handle unaligned access portably.

Process event timestamp requires eight byte alignment and its payload union must remain the final member, so inserting fields after it or packing the header breaks wire layout. Coredump request and acknowledgement versioning depends on explicit size fields, so peers must check sizes before reading newer fields, and capability second generation must not be used for new exchanges.

Conversions are symmetric inverses where applying host to foreign and back restores the original bit pattern, constant and runtime forms agree on values, and native order movement never changes bits. Masking an event selector with the aggregate never introduces bits outside the reportable set.

Telemetry flows follow subscription then notification. Control group statistics uses GET for synchronous query and NEW for asynchronous kernel events with distinct type and attribute namespaces. Process connector uses LISTEN to subscribe and IGNORE to unsubscribe, after which the kernel emits only subscribed event bits.
